solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Representative backing bankrupt college

indicators.note: backing means the representative's letters are read from the back, right to left

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament, an elected representative
bankrupt means broke, out of money

explanation.surface: A politician supports a college that has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MEP into PEM. PEMBROKE is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is the name of a college in both Oxford and Cambridge universities.

clue.text: Colour that is seen from below blue cover

indicators.note: in a down clue, viewing from the bottom reads the letters upwards, in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: A colour glimpsed from underneath a blue cover, like a bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from below' turns REDIE into EIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with duck feathers, a bed cover.

clue.text: Fruit that's British — a Granny Smith, primarily

parts.note: nana is an affectionate word for a grandmother

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word Smith is used

explanation.surface: A boast that a Granny Smith apple is a British fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny Smith' looks like the apple, but splits into Granny and the first letter of Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are a common tropical fruit, sold in yellow bunches.

clue.text: A solitary copper popped in at the right time

indicators.note: popped in means the copper is slipped inside the other piece

parts.note: a solitary one, a single one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A lone police officer dropped by just when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering on cue comes in exactly when signalled, so it means punctually, at the right moment.

clue.text: Be upset by start of boom or recession

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters of Be read upwards
start of means just the first letter of the word boom

explanation.surface: An economist's advice not to be upset by boom or bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BE into EB; 'boom or recession' poses as economics.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the tide going out, a retreat or receding, hence a recession.

clue.text: Interfere with power for male hawk

indicators.note: power for male means the power letter takes the place of the male letter

parts.note: to interfere is to meddle
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Meddling with authority on behalf of a hawkish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird or a war-monger but is the verb to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to sell them from place to place, a street trader's way of selling.

clue.text: Star and top journalist in opposing camps

parts.note: Polaris is the Pole Star
an editor, ED, is the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a leading reporter find themselves on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion that is polarised has split into two extreme opposing groups.

clue.text: Girl dressed up on a horse

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: robed means dressed
H stands for horse, slang for heroin, which is abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A girl in her finery sitting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' looks like one phrase but 'up' reverses ROBED to DEBOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah is a woman's first name, so it serves as a girl.

clue.text: Stories about source of money trees

indicators.note: about means the stories go round the other letter

parts.note: stories, as in falsehoods, are lies

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word money

explanation.surface: Tales about where the money trees come from.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime, or linden, is a tree, and citrus limes also grow on trees.

clue.text: God runs away from sculptor

indicators.note: away from means the runs letter leaves the sculptor's name

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A deity fleeing from an artist's studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Nothing found by European bachelor in search for weapon

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the search word

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
O, the figure zero, means nothing
a Balt is a European from the Baltic states

explanation.surface: A single European man's quest for a weapon turns up nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobalt bomb is a hypothetical nuclear weapon designed to spread radioactive fallout.

clue.text: Rogue overpricing very short opera

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: very cut short is V, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A rogue overcharges for a brief opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' rearranges OVERPRICING, but only after taking out the V that 'very short' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the opera by Borodin, famous for its Polovtsian Dances.

clue.text: Irish lad, lacking energy departs before long

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is missing from the word for departs

parts.note: departs means goes
E is the symbol for energy
before long means soon

explanation.surface: An Irish boy runs out of steam and soon leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossoon is an Irish word for a boy or young servant, from French garçon.

clue.text: Blackadder's last to take advantage of cunning plan

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the name Blackadder

parts.note: to take advantage of something is to use it

explanation.surface: Blackadder finally makes use of one of Baldrick's cunning plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackadder is the BBC sitcom where Baldrick always has 'a cunning plan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem, a scheme for deceiving someone.

clue.text: Relative dropping in repeatedly provides food

indicators.note: repeatedly means the shortened relative appears twice
dropping means the in letters are removed

parts.note: a cousin is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative who keeps popping round brings something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like visiting, but 'in' is dropped from COUSIN, leaving COUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina grains.

clue.text: Clear round left one unaware

indicators.note: round means the clear word goes around the other letters

parts.note: obvious means clear
I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: Someone left out, clearly ignorant of what is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means not noticing or not knowing what is going on around you.

clue.text: Group of artists in coach or train

definitions.meaning: a group of painters sharing a style, like the Flemish one
to coach or train someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: Painters travelling together by coach or by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of artists shares a style, and to school someone is to coach or train them.

clue.text: Original is like old material

indicators.note: original means creative or novel, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A fabric that is original yet looks old.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled silk is silk treated with oil to make it waterproof, a fabric used for capes.

clue.text: Juvenile delinquent stripped bare

indicators.note: delinquent means misbehaving, so the letters go astray and are rearranged
stripped means the outer letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: A young offender caught undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves UVENIL from Juvenile, which 'delinquent' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover or reveal it, used here as a verb.

clue.text: One chucks out intro for Eurovision winner

indicators.note: intro for means the first letter of the word Eurovision

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A singer is ejected right at the start of the Eurovision winner's song.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is someone who throws tenants out of a property.

clue.text: Numbers racket stopping exams

indicators.note: stopping means the racket plugs the middle of the exams word

parts.note: orals are spoken examinations
din means a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A numbers racket stopping students taking exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers racket' looks like illegal gambling; the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinals are numbers showing position in a sequence, such as first, second and third.

clue.text: Pointers not required? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: needless means not required

explanation.surface: A question of whether pointers are unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles on dials and compasses are pointers indicating a reading or direction.

clue.text: Bird that's most important we heard

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken, so the sound gives the answer

parts.note: most important means key, followed by we

explanation.surface: We heard which bird is the most important one.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless bird of New Zealand and its national emblem.

clue.text: Mad freebooter's severed head

indicators.note: severed head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a freebooter is a pirate

explanation.surface: A furious pirate's chopped-off head.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry is the same as irate, furious.

clue.text: Five visiting resort ordered red wine

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
someone visiting is in
Hove is a seaside resort on the English south coast, next to Brighton

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Visiting a resort with a few friends and ordering red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns RED into RDE. 'red wine' tempts, but vinho verde is a young wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinho verde is a young Portuguese wine, its name meaning green wine.

clue.text: Blooming sappers may be bizarre

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
sappers are military engineers; RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Bloody soldiers digging trenches may seem strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British swear word, but means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or eccentric, going beyond normal bounds.

clue.text: Resorted to cast iron drawer

indicators.note: resorted read as re-sorted means sorted again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turned to a cast iron chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but is someone who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist draws comic pictures, so is a drawer in the sense of one who draws.

clue.text: Gall from Sir Keith

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of the words Sir Keith

explanation.surface: Cheek from a knight called Keith.
explanation.definitionFit: To gall someone is to annoy or vex them.

clue.text: Cut in after old-fashioned look

indicators.note: after means the in letters follow the look word

parts.note: lo is an archaic word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Cutting in after a dated appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A loin is a cut of meat from the back of an animal.

clue.text: Revolutionary works for porcelain

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: works, as in functions or is useful, means serves

explanation.surface: Revolutionary artworks on porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sèvres is fine French porcelain made at the town of that name near Paris.

clue.text: Don't go off with drink as a souvenir

parts.note: food that does not go off keeps
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Stay and have a drink as a memento.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event.
